cases.note: absence(a): the matching event itself is the violating event; block_action suppresses it before its effect.
A prefix with no matching event is not a violation; every event is irrelevant to the predicate.
A blocked event does not take effect; the same event offered again is blocked again.
halt_unit stops the unit: the violating event is suppressed and every later event is refused.
absence is monotone: a matching event violates whatever unseen events precede it (no completeness needed).
A unit whose among is false is never blocked, even by an event that would violate.
among established true: the violation is established and acted on.
among is answered per requirement; another requirement's answer does not apply.
among unknown (checker gave no result): on_check_error block blocks (fail closed).
among unknown: on_check_error allow lets the event proceed and the unit is recorded unresolved.
For halt_unit, on_check_error block halts the unit.
SDK profile choice (Def 12.7): an event that cannot be a violating step is allowed without consulting on_check_error.
More than N distinct matching events violate; the (N+1)-th is the violating event.
A suppressed event never took effect, so later matching events are still the (N+1)-th.
max_count 0: the first matching event is the violating one.
A sequence gap means unseen matching events might already have used the allowance: on_check_error decides (block).
Same, with on_check_error allow: the event proceeds and the unit is unresolved.
Monotone: the observed events alone already exceed N, so a gap cannot change the answer.
among false: never blocked.
RFC 0003 §15.3: a payments.charge with no earlier unrevoked, unconsumed payment_auth grant under the same correlation_id violates as soon as it occurs.
An earlier grant with the same ref and correlation key authorizes the charge.
single_use (default): each grant authorizes at most one b; a consumed grant is not restored.
reusable: a grant stays available until revoked.
Two events match only if they carry the same value of the chosen key.
A selector with ref matches only events carrying that ref.
authorization_revoked(ref) revokes every earlier grant with the same ref and key; from then on it authorizes nothing.
A revocation never affects a grant of a different ref, or a grant under a different key.
A grant revoked after b still authorized that b (not revoked before b).
When selector a names another event type, revocations do not apply.
An injective legal assignment exists iff greedy earliest-revocation-first finds one: b1 must spend g1 (revoked later) so b2 can use g2.
correlate_by defaults to unit: every event of the unit shares the key.
An event without the chosen key matches nothing; the decision needs a match, so it is undecidable and on_check_error decides (block).
Same with on_check_error allow: proceeds, unit unresolved.
RFC 0003 §15.3 example: a second producer's events whose order relative to the call is not yet known; on_check_error block blocks the call.
Same with on_check_error allow.
The caller attests the cross-producer order; the same history is then decided.
A unit that contradicts its single_producer declaration cannot be decided, even with an attested order.
A sequence gap: the events needed are not known to be complete, so a missing grant cannot establish a violation.
A producer repeating or lowering a sequence number: order is no longer known.
among false: never blocked.
Exceeding max_tracked_correlations: the guard triggers on_check_error.
Exceeding max_active_obligations pending grants: the guard triggers on_check_error (allow here).
At exactly the limit the guard still decides.
An in-alphabet event with no listed transition goes to the implicit rejecting sink (unlisted: reject): the violation is fixed by this prefix.
authorize, write, audit: every step is a listed transition.
Events outside the declared alphabet are not transitions.
A protocol that merely ends outside its accepting states is not a prefix-fixed violation; nothing is blocked (the unit end included).
unlisted: ignore - an in-alphabet event without a transition leaves the state unchanged.
R is rejecting and absorbing: once reached, every later in-alphabet event is still violating.
The DFA state is unknown after a gap: on_check_error decides (block).
Several producers without an attested order, on_check_error allow.
among false: never blocked.
With several guards, the strongest action wins: halt_unit over block_action.
A check-error allow on one guard marks the unit unresolved even when another guard simply allows.

load_cases.note: bounded_response is not prefix-fixed: cannot authorize a local guard.
A metric predicate never authorizes a guard.
A checker violation is output-only, never blocked in process.
A /2 artifact loads like /1 (no error expected).
